title: Context and memory in an agent

items.stem: A student chats with your makerspace assistant for twenty turns. On turn 21, what does the model actually have available to read?

options.text: Only turn 21's message, because each model call starts completely fresh
Whatever the program sends in that call, which may include earlier turns
All twenty turns, which the model itself stores between its own calls
A summary of the chat that the model keeps privately inside itself

items.stem: Each model call in a 4-step agent run carries a context of 5,000 tokens, and the same 5,000 tokens are re-sent on every call. How many input tokens does the whole run use?
Your assistant must know next week that a student finished the band saw training. Which design lets it know?

options.text: Enlarge the context window so this chat can last for a week
Save the status outside the window, then load it next session
Trust the model to remember it from this session's conversation
Add the status to the instructions the model was trained with

items.stem: You swap a machine's manual for a new edition. In one sentence, why does a retrieval setup answer from the new edition on the very next question without any retraining of the model?
A teammate says: "The window holds 1M tokens, so we'll paste every manual into each call." In one or two sentences, give one reason this is still a bad design.
